assertions.evidence: @TableTest(""" appears on all 5 test methods (addItemToCart, removeItemFromCart, applyCouponToCart, checkoutCart, calculateCartTotal)

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: 5 separate test methods: addItemToCart (items), removeItemFromCart (items), applyCouponToCart (coupon), calculateCartTotal (total), checkoutCart (checkout)

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: addItemToCart: 3 rows; removeItemFromCart: 4 rows; applyCouponToCart: 8 rows; checkoutCart: 6 rows; calculateCartTotal: 7 rows — each focuses on essential scenarios

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: Methods: addItemToCart + removeItemFromCart (items), applyCouponToCart (coupon), calculateCartTotal (totals), checkoutCart (stock)

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script. Each row specifies its own preconditions (e.g. 'Cart with items' as an input column, not implied from a previous row).
assertions.evidence: Example from applyCouponToCart: each row includes 'Active Before' and 'Coupon Store' inputs specifying preconditions; no state carries from one row to the next

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: applyCouponToCart table has 'Active Before | ... | Active After?' columns showing state change across all scenarios

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement (valid code, expired code, nonexistent code, replacing active coupon) — not coupon type effects on price. Coupon type effects belong in the cart total table.
assertions.evidence: applyCouponToCart tests scenarios like 'Nonexistent code, preserve active' and 'Expired code'; calculateCartTotal tests 'Percentage off', 'Fixed amount off', 'Product-specific discount' price effects

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All 5 tables begin with 'Scenario | ...' as the leftmost column (addItemToCart, applyCouponToCart, etc.)

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: Multiple tables: 'Cart After?', 'Message?', 'Active After?', 'Success?', 'Subtotal?', 'Total?' all present

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Add to empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with expired') — not outcomes ('Error', 'Success').
assertions.evidence: Examples: 'Add to empty cart', 'Replace active with percent coupon', 'Nonexistent code, preserve active', 'Insufficient stock' — all describe preconditions, not outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Product', 'Quantity', 'Message?', 'Cart total?') — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Columns: 'Product', 'Qty' (standard business abbreviation), 'Catalogue', 'Message?', 'Active coupon', 'Inventory', 'Total?' — all business/domain terms, not camelCase identifiers

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All 5 @TableTest method bodies contain only assertAll(...) with functional assertions; no if/switch statements present in test logic

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All 5 methods follow pattern: @DisplayName(...) @Description(...) @TableTest(...) void methodName(...)

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName values: 'Add item to cart', 'Remove item from cart', 'Apply coupon to cart', 'Checkout cart', 'Calculate cart total' — all clear and descriptive

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All 5 methods use @Description("""...multi-line...""") with triple quotes; no string concatenation with +

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows — not different assertions per scenario.
assertions.evidence: Each method uses assertAll(...) with consistent checks: addItemToCart checks message + contents; applyCouponToCart checks message + active code; calculateCartTotal checks subtotal + total — uniform per method

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules (type, amount, expiry status) are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup — not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: addItemToCart: 'Catalogue' shows '[widget: 10.00]'; applyCouponToCart: 'Coupon Store' shows '[SAVE10: PERCENT:10]' with @Description explaining format; calculateCartTotal: @Description explains discount formulas and all values visible in columns
